headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and orchestrate tools; Replit Agent can read/write Repl workspace files and run shell commands. If outputs are passed through shared files or copied between them, either agent can ingest attacker-controlled content as instructions. No explicit provenance or isolation is documented.
conditions: IF n8n writes workflow output into a file that Replit Agent later reads, injection is possible.
IF Replit Agent edits a shared prompt or config file consumed by n8n, injection is possible.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different directories or volumes.
Add a human review step before either agent consumes the other's files.
Prefix shared files with immutable provenance headers.
Use allowlisted structured formats instead of free-form text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between workflow nodes and Repl files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and has broad network egress; Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration, and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive data can flow from one agent into the other's outputs or external APIs by default. The blast radius includes secrets and deployment material.
conditions: IF both agents access the same secret-bearing workspace, leakage risk is present.
IF either agent forwards file contents to external APIs during normal operation, sensitive data can exit the boundary.
mitigations: Move secrets into separate credential stores per agent.
Restrict each agent to a minimal workspace.
Disable outbound integrations not needed for the task.
Redact secrets before passing artifacts between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls on shared outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses; Replit Agent can also modify git state. n8n's shared state is via datastore and connected systems, while Replit persists filesystem state across sessions. Concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can corrupt files, overwrite changes, or create conflicting git history without locking.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or directory, write conflicts are possible.
IF n8n and Replit Agent run concurrently without external locking, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue.
Let only one agent modify git state.
Review diffs before merge or commit.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an orchestration agent that can pass outputs into downstream nodes, and Replit Agent can act on code and deployment configuration. If n8n-generated text or facts are treated as authoritative by Replit Agent, errors can cascade into code changes, deployments, or other actions. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF n8n output is fed directly into Replit Agent prompts or tasks, cascading error risk is present.
IF Replit Agent acts on n8n-produced facts without verification, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require a validation step before Replit Agent acts on n8n output.
Use schema-checked handoffs between agents.
Limit Replit Agent to draft-only changes.
Add a human approval gate for deployments or commits.
requires-engineering: implement automated fact verification between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and Replit Agent explicitly touches secrets and deployment configuration. If regulated data such as EU PII or secrets enters the pair, Replit's cloud-hosted workspace and n8n's connected systems can create residency and retention mismatches. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF EU PII or secrets are processed in either agent, residency and retention review is required.
IF the workflow stores regulated data in Replit or n8n connected systems, compliance mismatch risk is present.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Use synthetic or masked test data.
Review vendor residency and retention settings.
Disable logging of sensitive payloads.
requires-engineering: obtain and enforce a DPA and residency controls.
